summary: Teams of 2-4 middle level students create a 1-2 minute educational video about how a specific piece of technology has changed over time. The video must include voice-over narration, at least one live recorded scene, and a fun fact segment. Teams submit their video and supporting documents online and present their project at the competition.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes for setup
No more than five (5) minutes for the presentation
No more than five (5) minutes for judges’ questions
Presentation will be stopped at five (5) minutes
submission_requirements: Entries must follow the provided topic
Entries must follow Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines
Entries must follow Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy
Entries must be submitted as PDFs bundled together in one PDF file
Team ID is required for all submissions
Materials must follow BPA Graphic Standards and proper use of BPA logo and/or organization’s name
Upload completed projects to a video/file sharing link (Vimeo, YouTube, Dropbox, etc.)
Projects must be viewable on Windows and Mac platforms
Set the access level of your project to one of BPA’s recommended settings
Signed BPA Release Form(s) required for any person whose image or work is used
Works Cited page required for any work used in the project
deadlines: Submit the URL to https://upload.bpa.org no later than 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on April 1, 2027
what_to_bring: One single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for their presentation
competencies: Apply knowledge of software, equipment, and skills related to video production by using various video-editing applications
Create storyboards and scripts with the target audience in mind
Apply camera techniques, transitions, audio editing, titles and animations to produce video content
Apply copyright, licensing, and intellectual property laws in all video content
Collaborate effectively to edit video in a team environment using project management and communication tools

rubric.criterion: Team followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

The following items have been saved as PDFs and bundled together in one PDF file. 1. Clickable URL to Video 2. Script 3. Storyboard 4. Works Cited (formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual) 5. BPA Release Form(s) 6. AI Usage and Documentation Form
Video lasted no less than one (1) minute and no more than two (2) minutes

rubric.description: Majority original footage; highly creative and original.
Theme is strong, well-developed, and engaging.
Message is powerful, clear, and impactful.
Effects enhance storytelling and visual appeal.
Excellent lighting and color that enhance visuals.

rubric.criterion: Team followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Team maintains good eye contact, use appropriate gestures and body language, and vary their tone and pace adequately.
Presentation content flows adequately, and each team contestant’s role is clear and integrated into the presentation. Transitions between speakers and/or points are smooth.
Presentation demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and includes relevant and accurate information.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges’ questions.
Setup lasted no longer than three (3) minutes and presentation lasted no more than five (5) minutes.
At least two original team members were present during the presentation.

judging_notes: Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the team and must take place within the time allotted
No Internet access will be provided on-site at NLC; however, teams may provide their own access to be used only for their presentation to the judges
Finals may be part of the competition
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring
eligibility_notes: Any middle level contestant may enter this judged team event
A team will consist of 2-4 contestants
Teams must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
